messages:
anna: Heads-up — noticed a big regression after the eviction fanout change rolled yesterday. OOM spikes on a few busy pods, +2x eviction rate, and p99 token latency jumped. Anyone have quick thoughts? :grimacing:

mike: I think this is the classic LRU-shadowing problem. We promoted a handful of large KV entries and those end up evicting lots of small prompt prefixes. Cache churn goes up and warmup can't keep up.

suresh: Confirming from profiler — attaching a quick snapshot I pulled from prod pool-7. Not pretty.

suresh: ```
Profile snapshot (pool-7)
KV entries: 3.2M (small: 2.7M, large>1KB: 0.5M)
GPU reserved/used: 40.0G / 36.7G
Evictions/s (minute avg): 3.1k -> 6.4k (post-deploy)
TTL sweep latency: 95ms -> 260ms
KV miss P50/P95/P99: 2.1ms / 8.7ms / 28.4ms
Token generation p99: 210ms -> 410ms
Heap fragmentation estimate: 11% -> 27%
OOM events: 0 -> 4 (12h)
```

olivia: This matches what I saw during local repro. The fanout loop was increased so the TTL sweep touches more buckets per cycle. That improved cold cleanup but seems to cause eviction storms when combined with our single global LRU.

olivia: Current eviction worker is basically: ```
for bucket in pick_buckets(fanout):
  for entry in bucket.iter_evictable():
    if should_evict(entry): evict(entry)
```
Which does no size-awareness or per-size partitioning. Big entries are counted equally.

mike: Two quick mitigations: (1) add a small-size-first sweep (small prefixes have high reuse) and (2) implement a soft cap per-size-class so a single huge entry can't push out N small ones.

jia: Also important — batching/kernel selection effects. When short sequences dominate a worker, the runtime chooses a different kernel path that amplifies KV writes (more frequent context switches). Combined with the eviction fanout increase we end up with synchronized churn across shards. I can share traces if useful.

suresh: Traces would help. I also saw more frequent KV key collisions after we changed the key normalization for prompt-sources last month. Collisions cause multi-writes to the same slot, then a big evict chain tries to reinsert, which fragments memory.

olivia: Good catch. We should add a metric for "evict-churn-per-insert" — number of evictions triggered per successful insert. Right now we only track evictions/s which hides cascades.

deploy-bot: deploy: eviction-fanout v2 -> pool-7 (2026-03-16T09:18:21Z) :rocket:

anna: Action proposal: rollback the fanout bump on pool-7 -> revert to previous fanout=8, enable per-size soft-caps (small/med/large), add eviction-churn metric, and run a 1h soak with kernel-path telemetry enabled.

mike: I'll do the revert + metric in the next deploy window. I'll also add a quick guard: if evict-churn-per-insert > 3 for > 30s, throttle TTL sweep.

jia: I'll correlate kernel-path switches with churn. Hypothesis: when kernel switches > 40% of requests in a minute, churn spikes. If true, we can bias batching heuristics to stabilize kernel selection for a shard.

suresh: I'll prototype a per-size LRU split in the lab. Suggest sizes: tiny(<64B), small(64-256B), med(256-1KB), large(>1KB). Eviction policy: circular capacity weights [0.6,0.25,0.1,0.05] respectively.

olivia: For warmup, we should prefer prefetching tiny keys with a high fanout during low load, rather than sweeping all buckets equally. That reduces cold miss penalty for common paths.

mike: Quick commands I plan to run in canary: 
```
# revert fanout
rdctl config set runtime.kv.ttl_sweep.fanout 8 --scope pool-7
# enable metric
rdctl metrics enable runtime.kv.evict_churn_per_insert --scope pool-7
```

anna: SGTM. Owners: mike (revert + guard), suresh (per-size prototype), jia (kernel-path correlation), olivia (prefetch plan). Re-evaluate in 2 hours. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll put a short postmortem draft in #postmortems after we stabilize with the facts and timeline.

anna: If anyone sees new OOMs, ping me directly and I'll pause new canaries.

olivia: One more note — add a small ghost-list (like LRU-ghost) to track recently-evicted tiny keys. If ghost hits are high, that indicates we're evicting hot tiny keys and we should raise tiny cap.

suresh: copying the experiment checklist here:
 - revert fanout on pool-7 (mike)
 - enable evict-churn metric (mike)
 - prototype per-size lru (suresh)
 - kernel-path telemetry correlation (jia)
 - prefetch tiny-key-only plan (olivia)
 - postmortem + timeline (mike)

anna: Thanks team — let's keep comments short in this thread so we have a clear timeline.
